claim: Stars form inside large molecular clouds of gas and dust.
Cold molecular-cloud conditions help gas clump into denser pockets.
As dense clumps gather mass, gravity can make them collapse.
The earliest stage of the forming star is a protostar.
A protostar is fed by gas from its surrounding cloud.
Falling material can spiral into a rotating accretion disk.
The accretion disk feeds material onto the protostar.
As a protostar gains mass, its core compresses and gets closer to stable nuclear fusion.
Jets from a protostar's magnetic poles are part of the formation process.
Jets help carry away angular momentum so material can continue collecting.
